mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated interest rates compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates and reducing corporate borrowing capacity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 persons in the past month signals severe labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 100k in 1 month over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL above 205), a further increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened policy uncertainty and reduced risk appetite.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 205)
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 205), S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 5% signals weakening residential demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced construction activity and consumer confidence erosion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls > 5% in 1 month over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% and decline in real sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% in the past month signals broad-based supply-demand imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% and RSAFS falls > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO falls > 2% and RSAFS falls > 1% in 1 month over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real GDP (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong economic growth supports corporate earnings expansion and investor risk appetite.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 is above the 5-year average, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the Fed may accelerate rate hikes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0% over any 5-year rolling window, or the Rank IC over any 5-year rolling window is below 0.03.
